Following the release of iOS 26.6, iPadOS 26.6, and related software updates, Apple has detailed the extensive security patches included in today's new system versions.

Apple's security updates for iOS 26.6 and iPadOS 26.6 have a wide-ranging impact on iPhone and iPad

In iOS 26.6 and iPadOS 26.6, Apple has provided over 75 security patches for iPhone and iPad, covering multiple areas of the system.

More specifically, Apple's advisory contains 78 individual vulnerability entries, involving 87 unique CVE identifiers. As some entries involve more than one CVE, the number of CVEs is higher.

Apple has not indicated that any of the vulnerabilities patched in iOS 26.6 have been maliciously exploited in the wild.

Within Apple's lengthy list, several patches stand out:

  • A vulnerability in MediaRemote could allow an app to gain root privileges.
  • A vulnerability in AVEVideoEncoder could allow an app to execute arbitrary code with kernel privileges.
  • Vulnerabilities in Game Center and libc could allow a malicious app to escape sandbox restrictions.
  • A vulnerability in CloudAttestation could allow a malicious app to bypass code signing enforcement.
  • A vulnerability in ImageIO could lead to arbitrary code execution when processing a specially crafted malicious image.
  • Three vulnerabilities in SceneKit could lead to arbitrary code execution when processing specially crafted malicious files.
  • An Accessibility issue could leak sensitive data to a person with physical access via iPhone Mirroring output.
  • A Contacts vulnerability could allow an app to add contacts without user authorisation.

Kernel, WebKit, and Wi-Fi patches

Apple also patched over a dozen kernel vulnerabilities. Potential impacts include corrupting or writing to kernel memory, leaking kernel memory, bypassing network filters, and causing unexpected system termination.

WebKit also received a substantial number of patches. These vulnerabilities could expose process memory, leak whether a user has visited a particular link, enable interface spoofing, violate iframe sandbox rules, allow an app to read files outside its sandbox, or cause Safari to crash.

Another Wi-Fi vulnerability could allow a nearby attacker to corrupt process memory.

Beyond the 78 documented security patches, Apple has an "Additional Recognition" section listing 12 acknowledgements.

These entries are intended to thank researchers for their assistance, but are not listed as separate security patches and have not been assigned additional CVE identifiers.

The full patch list and researcher acknowledgements are available on Apple's website.

Security patches for Mac, Apple Watch, Apple TV, and Apple Vision Pro

Apple's newly released macOS Tahoe 26.6 security advisory lists 155 unique CVEs.

In addition to several patches shared with iPhone and iPad, the Mac update also addresses vulnerabilities that could allow an app to gain root privileges, escape the sandbox, bypass Gatekeeper checks or privacy preferences, and access protected data.

Apple also released security updates for older versions of macOS today, but these are not included in the counts in this article.

Apple has also detailed the patches in watchOS 26.6, tvOS 26.6, and visionOS 26.6. After excluding cross-platform overlaps, Apple's latest updates address a total of 194 unique CVEs.

Apple previously said that, in response to AI-powered attack tools, it has accelerated the release of its security patches, and brought forward last month's iOS 26.5.2 update.
